indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the word for a story wraps round the point

parts.note: a yarn is a story, especially a tall one
E, east, is one of the compass points

explanation.surface: A rambling tale that never gets to the point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, so YARN goes round E.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to crave or pine for it, a verb synonym.

definitions.meaning: fastenings for doors, a well-known make of cylinder fastening
jokingly, the hair on the heads of students at an American university in Connecticut

explanation.surface: College authorities are protected by security equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: Yale is an American university; locks are tresses of hair, which cover heads.
explanation.definitionFit: Yale is a brand of door fastening, and its students' hair would be their tresses.

indicators.note: beheaded says the first letter of the other deity's name is cut off

parts.note: another god: Mammon, the biblical god of riches

explanation.surface: One deity, and a second who has been decapitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' removes the first M of MAMMON.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammon, or Amun, was the chief deity of ancient Egypt, a ram-headed sun god.

clue.text: Making one point in tennis, uncommonly naughty they were

indicators.note: making in the sense of building, putting these letters together into a new arrangement

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
E, east, is one of the compass points

explanation.surface: Scoring in a tennis match, some players misbehaved badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making' shuffles I, E and TENNIS. The 1890s are remembered as the Naughty Nineties.
explanation.definitionFit: The final decade of the Victorian era earned a reputation for decadence and loose morals.

definitions.meaning: rescued, set free
having had the liver taken out, as an organ is moved elsewhere

explanation.surface: A patient whose life was rescued by a transplant operation.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the answer as DE-LIVERED, the liver removed, the question mark flagging the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Rescued people are delivered from danger; a body stripped of its liver is jokingly de-livered.

parts.note: a waterfall suggests a cascade, but the tiniest fall of water is a single drop from a tap

explanation.definitionFit: A single falling drop of liquid, as from a leaking tap, is the least water that can fall.

parts.note: the title of Virginia Woolf's 1927 novel names the destination of its characters' long-planned boat trip

explanation.definitionFit: Virginia Woolf's novel To the... names a coastal beacon tower as its goal.

clue.text: Under the state, girl is raised as a slave

indicators.note: in a down entry, under means this piece comes below the first

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for Virginia, a US state

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word is turned upwards, read from bottom to top

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Under the regime, a girl is brought up in servitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns LASS into SSAL, and 'Under' puts it below VA.
explanation.definitionFit: A vassal was a feudal tenant bound to a lord, hence a servant or subordinate.

clue.text: Score with a stage version of " The Vagabonds "

parts.note: a run is a score in cricket

indicators.note: version says the letters of a stage are reworked into another form

explanation.surface: A musical score accompanies a theatre production of a play about tramps.
explanation.definitionFit: Runagate is an archaic word for a wanderer or fugitive, a vagrant.

clue.text: Old coin found by foreign nobleman at last

indicators.note: last says the small word comes at the end of the answer

parts.note: duc is the French for duke

explanation.surface: An antique coin turns up beside a foreign aristocrat after a long search.
explanation.definitionFit: A ducat was a gold or silver coin formerly used across Europe.

parts.note: keener looks like a comparative of keen, eager, but a keener is a mourner who wails over the dead

explanation.definitionFit: To keen is to wail in grief at a funeral, so a keener's activity is mourning aloud.

clue.text: Sort of boom with the younger generation in charge

parts.note: a son is of the generation after his parent

explanation.surface: A noisy economic boom with young people running things.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonic boom is the bang made by an aircraft passing the speed of sound.

clue.text: Perhaps I'm prone to measure mine

definitions.text: Perhaps I'm prone to measure mine

parts.words: Perhaps I'm prone to measure mine
parts.note: prone looks like inclined to, but it means lying flat on the ground, the way someone who falls is said to measure their size along it

explanation.definitionFit: A person who falls flat is said to measure their length on the ground, the idiom behind the clue.

clue.text: Honest view about art, if retrograde

indicators.note: about tells us the word for view goes round the other piece

parts.note: a sight is a view

indicators.note: retrograde means moving backwards, so the word art is read in reverse

explanation.surface: An honest opinion of art that harks back to the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if retrograde' turns ART into TRA, which 'about' puts inside SIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight means frank and truthful, as in a straight answer.

definitions.meaning: Robin is the first name of the tailor among Shakespeare's rustics in A Midsummer Night's Dream
half-starved, thin from want of food
in the rustics' play, the tailor takes the part of the Moon

explanation.surface: A hungry robin on a moonlit night.
explanation.walkthrough: Robin is the rustic tailor in A Midsummer Night's Dream who plays Moonshine in Pyramus and Thisbe.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tailor bears the surname, which also means a starving creature, and he plays Moonshine.

definitions.meaning: a custom or accepted way of doing things
a large formal gathering of delegates or members

explanation.surface: A gathering of the fashion world, such as a trade show.
explanation.definitionFit: A custom or usage is a convention, and so is a formal conference such as a party gathering.

parts.note: main course suggests a dinner, but the main is the open sea and the course is a ship's heading

explanation.definitionFit: A ship's officer who plots the route across the sea advises which heading to take.

indicators.note: tailless says the final letter of the animal's name is dropped

parts.note: the ermine is the stoat in its white winter coat

explanation.surface: A stoat with no tail turns up on someone's doorstep.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoa is a covered colonnade or portico in Greek architecture, a kind of porch.

definitions.meaning: a pledge or guarantee
self-..., a firm belief in oneself

explanation.surface: A pledge that reassures us.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm guarantee is an assurance, and poise or self-belief is also called this.

definitions.meaning: sums of money paid ahead of time
the amorous overtures of a seducer

explanation.surface: A famous seducer hands out money.
explanation.definitionFit: Money paid up front are sums lent ahead, and a seducer's passes at women are romantic approaches.

clue.text: This god returns to, the notice of Frenchmen

indicators.note: returns says the French word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: avis is the French for notice

explanation.surface: A deity comes back to the attention of the French.
explanation.definitionFit: Siva, also spelt Shiva, is a principal Hindu deity, the destroyer.

parts.note: metric looks like metres and grams, but it is the metre of verse, so these are students of versification

explanation.definitionFit: Prosody is the study of verse rhythm and metre, and its scholars are specialists in poetic metre.

clue.text: Ten numbers put up in fourteen lines

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the run of letters is turned to read upwards

explanation.surface: Ten figures are displayed over fourteen rows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns TEN + NOS, TENNOS, upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonnet is a poem of fourteen lines with a set rhyme scheme.

clue.text: Firm has man in Zurich — North is the name

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
the gnomes of Zurich are Swiss bankers

explanation.surface: A company employs a Swiss banker who goes by the name North.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'gnomes of Zurich' was a 1960s nickname for Swiss bankers.
explanation.definitionFit: A cognomen is a surname or nickname, originally a Roman family designation.

definitions.meaning: young male horses
jokingly, revolvers made by an American gunsmith, which are loaded with bullets

explanation.surface: Horses carried heavy packs.
explanation.definitionFit: Young male horses share their name with the famous make of revolver, a gun that is loaded.

definitions.meaning: rapid gabble or chatter
jokingly, one who gives a jab, an injection for a local anaesthetic

explanation.surface: Chatting quickly with the anaesthetist at the local hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast, unclear speech is jabber, and a person who jabs a needle is jokingly a jabber.

parts.note: a tot looks like a dram of whisky, but it is a small child, and Scotch means Scottish

explanation.definitionFit: Bairn is the Scots word for a child.

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A Spanish man from the city of the Alhambra, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the first man was created from dust, and his name stands for mankind.

parts.note: L stands for libra, a pound, the price asked
canned goods come in a tin, giving 'a tin'

explanation.surface: A diner asks how much the tinned tongue costs.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 'what price canned?' is '£ a tin', L being the pound sign; 'tongue' is a language, not the meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin is a language, and tongue is an old word for a language.

definitions.meaning: the formal placing of someone in an office or post
producing an electric current by a changing magnetic field

explanation.surface: Putting in equipment to supply power.
explanation.definitionFit: A new vicar's ceremonial admission is his induction; electromagnetic induction generates current.

clue.text: Layers get Meg to back by a trick

parts.note: strata are layers, as of rock

indicators.note: to back means the name is run backwards

explanation.surface: Meg is asked to support someone through a deceitful plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratagem is a scheme or ruse designed to deceive.

definitions.meaning: sight is one example of the five faculties
the import or significance of words

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether they have grasped what is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Sight is one of the bodily faculties, and the gist of a sentence is its import, both senses of the word.
